q: A container in a pod crashes and is restarted by the kubelet. What happens to data in the pod's `emptyDir` volume?
options: It is wiped, because emptyDir is tied to the container
It is kept only if `medium: Memory` is set
It is copied to a PersistentVolume
It is kept; emptyDir lives as long as the pod, and is deleted only when the pod is removed from the node
explain: emptyDir has pod lifetime. Container restarts keep it; deleting the pod (or eviction/rescheduling) destroys it. `medium: Memory` just backs it with tmpfs.

q: You create a PVC on kind and it stays `Pending` with the event `waiting for first consumer to be created before binding`. What should you do?
options: Delete it and switch to `Immediate` binding
Nothing is wrong: with `WaitForFirstConsumer`, the volume is provisioned when a pod using the PVC is scheduled
Install a CSI driver
Create a PV manually
explain: `WaitForFirstConsumer` delays provisioning until the scheduler picks a node, so the volume is created in the right node/zone. Create the pod and the PVC binds.

q: On EKS, a pod using a gp3 EBS volume with `volumeBindingMode: Immediate` stays Pending with `volume node affinity conflict`. What is the most likely cause?
options: gp3 does not support Kubernetes
The PVC requested ReadWriteMany
The volume was provisioned in an AZ where no schedulable node can run the pod; EBS volumes are zonal
The kubelet lacks IAM permissions
explain: With `Immediate`, the disk is created before scheduling, possibly in an AZ that does not fit the pod (resources, affinity, taints). `WaitForFirstConsumer` avoids this by provisioning after scheduling.

q: Which statements about access modes are true? (select all)
options: `ReadWriteOnce` allows multiple pods on the same node to mount the volume read-write
`ReadWriteOncePod` restricts the volume to a single pod in the cluster
EBS volumes support `ReadWriteMany` across AZs
Amazon EFS is a typical choice for `ReadWriteMany`
explain: RWO is per node, RWOP per pod. EBS is RWO and zonal; for RWX use a shared filesystem such as EFS (NFS).

q: A PVC whose PV has reclaim policy `Delete` is deleted. What happens?
options: The PV and the underlying disk are deleted
The PV becomes `Released` and the data stays
The PV is recycled with `rm -rf` and made available
Nothing until the namespace is deleted
explain: `Delete` removes the PV and the backing storage. `Retain` keeps both (PV goes to `Released`). `Recycle` is deprecated.

q: A retained PV is `Released`. A new PVC that matches it stays `Pending`. Why?
options: Retained PVs can never be reused
The reclaim policy must be changed to `Delete` first
The new PVC must be in the `default` namespace
The PV still has a `spec.claimRef` pointing to the old claim; an admin must remove it to make the PV `Available`
explain: Kubernetes refuses to hand old data to a new claim automatically. Removing `claimRef` (after deciding the data can be reused or wiping it) makes the PV bindable again.

q: You scale a PostgreSQL StatefulSet from 1 to 3 replicas. What do `postgres-1` and `postgres-2` contain?
options: Streaming replicas of `postgres-0`
Independent, freshly initialised databases on their own new PVCs
Copies of `postgres-0`'s disk made by Kubernetes
Nothing; StatefulSets cannot scale databases
explain: StatefulSets give stable names and per-replica PVCs but know nothing about Postgres replication. Operators such as CloudNativePG handle replication, failover and backups.

q: A `postgres:18` StatefulSet mounts its PVC at `/var/lib/postgresql/data` (the path used up to PostgreSQL 17). What happens?
options: The image's entrypoint detects the mount at the old path and exits with an error about the 18+ data layout; mount at `/var/lib/postgresql` instead
It works the same as before
Postgres automatically migrates the data
The PVC is resized
explain: PostgreSQL 18 images use `PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/18/docker` and declare `/var/lib/postgresql` as the volume. The entrypoint refuses to run with a mount at the old path, to prevent writing data outside the volume.

q: A worker app writes to `/var/media`, but its PVC is mounted at `/media`. What symptom do you expect?
options: `CreateContainerConfigError`
The pod stays Pending
Everything appears to work, but data is lost whenever the pod is replaced
The kubelet refuses to mount the volume
explain: Writes go to the container's ephemeral writable layer. Nothing fails until the pod is recreated. Verify persistence with `df -h <path>` and a restart test.

q: A Deployment with `replicas: 1`, `strategy: RollingUpdate` and an RWO EBS PVC gets stuck during a rollout with `Multi-Attach error`. Which fixes are appropriate? (select all)
options: Use `strategy: Recreate` so the old pod releases the volume first
Use a StatefulSet
Increase `maxSurge` to 2
Switch the PVC access mode to `ReadWriteMany` on the same EBS StorageClass
explain: RollingUpdate starts the new pod before the old one stops; if it lands on another node, the RWO volume is still attached elsewhere. Recreate or a StatefulSet (which replaces pods one by one, old first) avoids that. EBS does not support RWX, and more surge makes it worse.

q: What is the role of a CSI node plugin?
options: It creates disks through the cloud API
It takes VolumeSnapshots
It schedules pods close to their volumes
It runs on every node (DaemonSet) and formats/mounts volumes into pods when the kubelet asks
explain: The controller plugin (with sidecars like external-provisioner/attacher/resizer/snapshotter) talks to the storage API; the node plugin handles stage/publish (format and mount) on each node.

q: Which statement about VolumeSnapshots is correct?
options: They work with any StorageClass, including kind's local-path
They require the snapshot CRDs and controller plus a CSI driver with snapshot support, and give crash-consistent copies
They are application-consistent for databases by default
They replace the need for `pg_dump` and WAL archiving
explain: Snapshots need CSI support (local-path has none). They are crash-consistent; databases recover via WAL replay, but you still want logical dumps and point-in-time recovery for a complete strategy.

q: Your team asks whether to run the production PostgreSQL for `shipit` in your EKS cluster. Which answer best reflects good practice?
options: Always run it in Kubernetes; managed databases are legacy
A plain StatefulSet with 3 replicas gives you HA for free
Prefer RDS/Aurora unless you need portability, many small databases, or tighter cost control and can operate it; if you run it in-cluster, use an operator like CloudNativePG with off-cluster backups
Never run any database on Kubernetes
explain: Operators make in-cluster databases viable, but you own upgrades, backups, restores and on-call. Managed services shift that burden. The right choice depends on requirements and skills.
